decisions.reason: As a niche particle-therapy water phantom it carries higher rationalization risk than routine chamber products, but it still supports the firm's advanced QA positioning and should be kept unless demand proves persistently weak.

This small-volume ionization chamber faces some overlap and portfolio-crowding risk, yet it remains a relevant measurement tool within the firm's core dosimetry offering and is more likely to stay than be withdrawn.
A standard clinical ionization chamber family with several models is a core revenue and service platform product, so management would normally continue it rather than remove it.
An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry fits everyday radiotherapy QA workflows well and should remain on the market as part of the firm's integrated hardware-software-service business.
A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional, widely usable clinical product that complements the established chamber portfolio and is therefore likely to be retained.
